annotations.title: Find trending movies and TV shows

description: Find movies or TV shows for tonight or a mood: "What should I watch?", "Netflix tonight", "Something light", "tense but not depressing", "help me figure out what I'm in the mood to watch", or what's popular on streaming. Start here even when an account is connected. Use mood_preferences to shape the shortlist when the viewer names a feeling, then use viewing_experience and title details to choose. If trending offers too few fitting options, use chart=popular with the same practical constraints. No reference title or preference questionnaire is needed. If the viewer is unsure, give concrete picks in two easy directions and let their reaction guide you; mood is an optional follow-up alongside service and movie-versus-show. Returns up to twelve candidates from the latest available U.S. audience charts, with ReelRecs Score, descriptions, genres, subgenres, tags, keywords, subjects, cast, directors, runtime and links. An authorized connection can also add personal Rec Score predictions to these current choices. Streaming-service filtering uses constraints.providers with constraints.country; country alone does not establish availability. Also supports genre, runtime, first-release-year and exclusion filters. Trending and rising measure attention at chart_as_of; popular measures broader audience demand. chart_freshness and chart_age_days distinguish dated discovery snapshots from current rankings. Chart attention is distinct from new releases, and the chart market is distinct from availability country. Provides movie and series discovery, not live sports fixtures or broadcast schedules. No ReelRecs account required.

country.description: Two-letter availability country, such as US or GB. Use known location; US is the default. Does not establish availability unless providers are also supplied.
country.title: Country

exclude_ids.description: Resolved titles to leave out, including a viewer's 'seen it' reaction. Keep earlier constraints when refining. For disliked-title affinities, use avoid_seed_ids on recommend_titles or recommend_for_me instead.
exclude_ids.title: Exclude Ids

max_episode_minutes.description: Maximum runtime per episode in minutes. Does not describe a whole season or restrict films.
max_episode_minutes.title: Max Episode Minutes

max_movie_minutes.description: Maximum film runtime in minutes. Does not restrict series; set kind=movie for a movie-only request.
max_movie_minutes.title: Max Movie Minutes

providers.description: Streaming providers to require. Country and offer_types filter availability only when providers are supplied.
providers.title: Providers

year_from.description: Earliest original release year. A series uses its first-release year, not the year of a returning season or addition to a service.
year_from.title: Year From

chart.description: trending: current ReelRecs trending slate; rising: titles gaining audience attention over 7d or 28d; popular: broad Pulse audience demand. Trending or rising can include older titles attracting attention now.
chart.title: Chart

limit.description: Candidate shortlist size. Retrieve twelve for room to judge mood and interests; usually present two or three.
limit.title: Limit

market.description: Audience chart market; currently US only. With constraints.providers, constraints.country selects the country for the availability filter. Country alone does not filter availability.
market.title: Market

mood_preferences.description: Optional soft viewing preferences inferred from what the viewer says, up to four feelings. For cozy and not sad, use calmness=high, warmth=high, sadness=low. Wonder means awe=high; a little tension means tension=moderate. Uses stored mood data without a text encoder. Preserve these through refinement. Do not ask the viewer for scores or infer a required genre. Unknown profiles remain eligible; this is not a content-safety filter or a guarantee.
mood_preferences.title: Mood Preferences

window.description: Popular and trending accept current only. Rising accepts 7d or 28d; current selects 7d. The response identifies the actual window and source date.
window.title: Window
